subject: FinTrack POC: on-ramp integration & acceptance checklist
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>

Subject: FinTrack POC: on-ramp integration & acceptance checklist

Hi Emma — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned before the technical kickoff.

TL;DR: FinTrack wants a 3-week POC that demonstrates: 1) end-to-end SDK integration (text generation + streaming responses), 2) stable latency under the sample QPS, and 3) quality parity against your internal baseline on the 200-case eval set. Ownership and a proposed timeline below.

Success criteria (from our conversation):
- Functional: API routes instrumented for chat and tool-calling (generate, stream, toolcall) integrated into your sandbox services.
- Performance: 95th-token-latency < 300ms at 20 concurrent sessions (simulated traffic).
- Quality: F1/ROUGE metrics within 5% of your baseline across the 200-case eval set.
- Observability: per-request tracing and token-level cost reporting visible in Redwood Console.

Proposed high-level timeline (3 weeks):
Week 0 (this week): kickoff + access and test data share.
Week 1: SDK integration + API route wiring; streaming validation.
Week 2: Load runs, quality evals, tweak quant/ batching profiles.
Week 3: Acceptance run and handing over dev artifacts.

Owners (internal / FinTrack):
- Redwood technical lead: Marcus Lin (marcus.lin@redwood.com) — SDK handoff, streaming tuning, load tests.
- CS / program manager: Vanessa Ortiz (vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com) — timelines, weekly check-ins, acceptance sign-off.
- FinTrack technical lead: Rajesh Menon (rajesh.menon@fintrack.com) — sandbox access, integrating API routes, collecting eval sets.

I’ve attached a first-pass success-criteria spreadsheet and an API mapping doc. Can you confirm the acceptance criteria above and whether your team can commit to sandbox access and the 200-case eval set by Thursday? Once you confirm, Marcus will share a technical runbook and we’ll schedule the kickoff for next Monday.

Thanks,
Irene Choi

Hi Irene — thanks for the clear recap. This matches what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side before the kickoff: 

1) Eval set: we can provide the 200-case eval set by Thursday EOD. Will provide labels and the baseline scores.
2) Sandbox access: we can open an IP allow-list for Redwood’s staging IPs and provide API keys to your team; Rajesh will coordinate.
3) Streaming & tool-calling: we need to confirm how Redwood’s streaming connections handle reconnects and toolcall metadata headers (we need request_id and trace_id passed through). Can Marcus call out specific headers or SDK hooks?
4) Security/compliance: SOC2 evidence is in motion; we’ll need the audit log export format for your private deployment option (for legal) but for the POC, standard Console access is fine.

We’re comfortable with the 3-week cadence. Please send the technical runbook and any lightweight smoke-test scripts so our backend team can prep. Also, can you include an estimate of the expected token cost for a 1k-requests smoke run so we can budget for the trial credits?

Subject: Re: FinTrack POC: on-ramp integration & acceptance checklist — tech runbook + API mapping

Hi team — following up with a technical plan and specifics Emma asked for. I’m attaching the runbook and a compact API mapping doc (also uploaded to the Drive link Irene shared). Below are the key integration steps, owners, and a smoke-test checklist.

Technical summary: Redwood exposes REST endpoints for synchronous generate and a streaming websocket for incremental tokens. SDKs (Python/Node) provide high-level primitives that manage reconnects and token buffering. Tool-calling is supported via a structured 'tool_call' field in the response envelope; metadata headers (x-rw-request-id, x-rw-trace-id) are preserved end-to-end and surfaced in the Console.

Integration steps (detailed):
1) Sandbox access & auth (Rajesh / Redwood infra) — Redwood will provide API keys scoped to the sandbox project. Expected dev time: 0.5 days.
2) SDK install & demo app (Marcus) — pip/npm package + example chat client. Expected dev time: 1 day.
3) Wire API routes (FinTrack) — map your /api/chat endpoint to call Redwood generate/stream routes; include tokenization guard rails. Expected dev time: 2 days.
4) Tool-calling flow (joint) — implement tool_call handler that receives structured tool payloads, calls internal services, and returns structured outputs. Redwood SDK includes a callback helper: on_tool_call(meta, payload) — Marcus will demo. Expected dev time: 2 days.
5) Streaming validation & reconnects — SDK automatically replays up to last-seen token on transient disconnects; application must attach x-rw-request-id. Expected dev time: 1 day.
6) Load tests & profiling (Redwood + FinTrack) — run orchestrated load using our test harness; capture 95th-token latencies. Expected dev time: 2 days.
7) Eval run & acceptance (joint) — run the 200-case eval set and compare metrics. Expected dev time: 1 day.

Smoke-test checklist (what to run the first day):
- Install SDK and run example chat (verify token stream arrives and console traces appear).
- Trigger a tool_call and validate payload roundtrip and tool metadata.
- Run 100-sample latency probe and confirm baseline < 300ms median.

Headers / metadata to include (required):
- x-rw-request-id: unique request id (must be passed by FinTrack)
- x-rw-trace-id: optional trace id for distributed tracing
- x-rw-environment: sandbox

Token cost estimate (1k-request smoke run):
- Typical request size for your sandbox: ~120 input tokens, avg 80 output tokens => ~200 tokens total.
- Estimated cost: 1k * 200 tokens = 200k tokens. Under the trial profile we discussed, this maps to ~USD 18 of credit (rough estimate; Marcus will provide exact price per model variant in the kickoff).

Artifacts attached: redwood-api-mapping.md (API route examples and request/response samples), streaming-integration-diagram.png (handoff flow), fintrack-poc-success-criteria.xlsx (detailed acceptance matrix).

Marcus Lin
